x: Harry Churcher once again won the Business Houses 2 Miles Track Championship, with Bob McMullen 2nd and at the same meeting young Dan Godfrey won the 100 and 200 Youths' events. Vern Blowfield won the 1 mile title when beating Stan Cox, the Olympic Games runner.

This was held at Parliament Hill on November 29th, and we had a number of our members competing in a field of just over 100 runners. Martin Whenman, who is a second-claim member, was first home in 30m. 10s., and he beat S.
The second annual race was held at Wimbledon on June 27th, and we had received a good entry, which comprised most of the leading road men, with the exception of Jim Peters and Stan Cox.

It was very pleasing to see the return to true form of Eric Gebbett in this race, in which, although never in the front against such fine performers as Stan Cox and Geoff Iden, turned in the best performance of his career to finish 6th in a time which would have won him many a race over this course.
Heywood scored a runaway victory from Barrett of Ealing with Eldon taking third place inside Stan Cox's record of 54.19. Dave Baulch finished 4th, 9 secs outside the previous record.
